newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty seen buoyed by foreign fixed bond buying.
newsitem.headline: Zloty seen buoyed by foreign fixed bond buying.

text.p: Foreign bids at today's 800 million zloty Polish fixed bond tender may propell the zloty past central bank-guarded levels at 2.5 percent from the parity rate and set off a currency buying intervention, dealers said.

They said foreign demand at the auction could total between 500 and 700 million zlotys, driving the zloty up, as the value date for today's forex spot transactions and the payment date for bonds were both on May 12.
"Large foreign entry at the bond tender could push the zloty up and trigger a central bank intervention," said Andrzej Rzysko of Societe Generale in Warsaw.

At 0735 GMT the zloty was at 2.47/2.44 percent from the trading band centre against 2.49/2.43 percent at opening. It was at 3.1605/10 against the dollar and 1.8338/43 against the mark from 3.1600/20 and 1.8340/50 at opening respectively.

Dealers said the 15-percent two-year bonds and 12-percent five-year paper were highly attractive to investors because of Poland's good fundamentals and their yields were expected to ease amid high demand to around 21.0 percent and 18.4 percent.
At the last tender in April the average yields of the bonds, maturing on June 12, 1999 and June 12, 2002 were at 21.4 percent and 18.5 percent, respectively.

On the money market one-day rates were expected to ease to around 23 percent at offer later today from 22.60/23.55 for overnight and 22.70/23.20 for tomorrow next cash on a net inflow of 2.2 billion zlotys into the system today.
Dealers did not expect the central bank to stage any draining operations on Wednesday.
